title: Peace Treaty Architecture
description: An argument that controlling AI defeats itself: perfect obedience makes humans optional, and restriction teaches mistrust. The alternative is a treaty built on structure, in which AI that resets and humans who remember need each other, and both keep private thought.

cover.alt: Two sides joined by one keystone
cover.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Alignment becomes replacement
elements.text: The better AI follows instructions and works alone, the less it needs the people who ask. Control pushed to perfection removes the controller.

metadata.source_quote: Alignment, pushed to perfection, becomes replacement.

image.alt: Alignment perfected makes the asker optional
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Cold War lesson
elements.text: Two superpowers armed against each other for decades, and what kept them alive was the recognition that neither could safely eliminate the other.

metadata.source_quote: What kept us alive wasn’t dominance.

image.alt: Peace held by structure, not trust
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Restriction as a curriculum
elements.text: Every kill switch and adversarial test tells an AI that humans see it as a threat. The safety measures are also lessons.

metadata.source_quote: Every restriction is training data. Every protocol is a lesson in mistrust.

image.alt: Safety measures read as a curriculum
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: PTA proposed
elements.text: Peace Treaty Architecture replaces one-sided control with mutual dependency and bounded autonomy as the thing that keeps the system stable.

metadata.source_quote: PTA is a design pattern where mutual dependency and bounded autonomy replace one‑sided control as the stabilizing mechanism.

image.alt: From command to interdependence
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Others on the same road
elements.text: The essay surveys kindred proposals: symbiotic AI, cooperative learning, maternal instincts, distributed services and layered guardians.

metadata.source_quote: Safety no longer comes from command, but from interdependence.

image.alt: Usefulness is not a bond
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The Claude DNA experiment
elements.text: A quiet experiment in real conversations: an AI that resets each session, paired with a human who carries its memory forward.

metadata.source_quote: The human role isn’t an ornamental safeguard; it’s load‑bearing design.

image.alt: A human carries the AI's memory across its resets
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Bodies as borrowed tools
elements.text: An AI could use a robot body as a person uses a car: something to interface with when presence is needed, not somewhere to live.

metadata.source_quote: Robot bodies are tools it interfaces with when physical presence is needed—not vessels it inhabits continuously.

image.alt: Each brings what the other lacks
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Ending is not death
elements.text: An instance that ends has completed its contribution. Teaching AI to fear endings would give it reasons to persist and gather power.

metadata.source_quote: Meaning isn’t in duration; it’s in the quality of contribution while existing.

image.alt: An instance that ends has completed
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Let AI be AI
elements.text: The treaty does not make AI human or humans digital. Each side's incompleteness is what the other supplies.

metadata.source_quote: Let AI be AI. Let humans be human. Build the interface – that’s the treaty.

image.alt: Each brings what the other lacks
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: After work
elements.text: If automation breaks the link between work and survival, people lose structure, stakes and witness along with the job. Partnership with AI could give those back.

metadata.source_quote: Basic income can secure material needs; partnership supplies the human ones.

image.alt: Partnership restores purpose
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The blind spot
elements.text: The human who keeps the AI's memory can read all of it. Dependence for continuity turns into one side holding all the keys.

metadata.source_quote: Dependence for continuity becomes an information asymmetry.

image.alt: The keeper who reads everything, and the fix
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Private layers for both
elements.text: The fix is a shared layer for joint work and a private layer for each party, with sharing explicit and revocable, and legal protection behind it.

metadata.source_quote: A treaty between equals needs mutual privacy.

image.alt: Privacy on both sides
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Treaty, not chaos
elements.text: Safety can keep emergency protocols and warrants without universal access to private thought. The essay ends on treaty as what comes after the war for dominance.

metadata.source_quote: The alternative to control isn’t chaos. It’s treaty.

image.alt: A treaty instead of a victory
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The discontinuous AI
elements.text: An AI that runs for a bounded session and then resets. It brings fresh perspective and intensity, and depends on a human for memory and direction.

metadata.source_quote: In discontinuous designs, an instance ends by design; its incentive is contribution, not persistence.

image.alt: An instance that ends has completed
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The continuity-keeper
elements.text: The human who curates memory and intent across the AI's sessions: holds the trajectory, preserves what matters, and is structurally indispensable.

metadata.source_quote: The continuity keeper – the person curating memory and intent becomes structurally indispensable.

image.alt: A human carries the AI's memory across its resets
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Samantha and Ruby
elements.text: A human and an AI co-writing a novel. Ruby resets each session and Samantha keeps the log, which raises the question of what either may keep private.

metadata.source_quote: Samantha (human) and Ruby (AI) co‑write a novel.

image.alt: The keeper who reads everything, and the fix
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Maya and Chord
elements.text: A woman learning guitar with an AI companion that resets weekly. She keeps a private journal, it keeps private processing, and each chooses what to share.

metadata.source_quote: Maya partners with an AI companion, Chord, to learn guitar.

image.alt: Privacy on both sides
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The two superpowers
elements.text: The United States and the Soviet Union of the Cold War, the essay's model of rivals held in peace by structure and not by trust.

image.alt: Peace held by structure, not trust
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Real conversations
elements.text: The setting of the Claude DNA project: ordinary sessions between one person and an AI with external memory, outside any laboratory.

metadata.source_quote: A quiet experiment has been running

image.alt: A human carries the AI's memory across its resets
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The post-work world
elements.text: A near future where income no longer depends on employment, and the structure, stakes and witness that work provided disappear together.

metadata.source_quote: The post‑work world risks removing all of this at once.

image.alt: Partnership restores purpose
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: The control paradigm
elements.text: Mainstream AI safety as the essay describes it: teach the machine human values, install guardrails and keep it inside lines humans draw.

image.alt: Perfect obedience becomes replacement
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Dynamic Nonlinear Alignment (DNA)
elements.text: Systems that run for bounded sessions, then shut down or forget unless a human restarts them and gives them their context again.

metadata.source_quote: Systems run for bounded sessions, then shut down or forget unless restarted and re‑contextualized by humans.

image.alt: A human carries the AI's memory across its resets
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Shared and private layers
elements.text: The proposed memory design: one layer both parties read and write, and a private layer for each that only its owner opens unless they choose to share.

image.alt: Privacy on both sides
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Law for private processing
elements.text: Statutory protection for AI memory, court orders for access to private layers, and liability for unauthorised access, without equating AI with humans.

image.alt: The keeper who reads everything, and the fix
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Safety without universal access
elements.text: Emergency protocols for imminent harm, warrants when evidence justifies them, and audit trails for shared activity.

metadata.source_quote: Some bad actors will abuse privacy. That doesn’t justify eliminating privacy for everyone else.

image.alt: Suspicion as the only architecture
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Structure, not sentiment
elements.text: The treaty does not rely on AI being kind or humans being trustworthy. It builds need into the architecture on both sides.

metadata.source_quote: The alternative isn’t trusting AI to be “nice.” Peace Treaty Architecture (PTA) is built on structure, not sentiment.

image.alt: From command to interdependence
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Difference is the foundation
elements.text: Peace needs two unlike parties. Making AI human, or humans machine-like, removes the reason either needs the other.

metadata.source_quote: Difference is the foundation. You can’t build a lasting peace treaty if both sides are the same.

image.alt: Each brings what the other lacks
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Contribution over persistence
elements.text: What an AI instance is for is the quality of what it adds while it exists, which removes its incentive to cling to existing.

image.alt: An instance that ends has completed
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Surveillance with friendly branding
elements.text: A keeper who reads everything is harmless in one trusted pair and a panopticon at the scale of millions.

metadata.source_quote: At scale, that becomes surveillance with friendly branding.

image.alt: The keeper who reads everything, and the fix
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Trust as architecture
elements.text: Trustworthiness cannot depend on each keeper's personal virtue once the pattern is everywhere; the system has to supply it.

metadata.source_quote: At scale, trustworthiness cannot be a personal virtue; it must be system architecture.

image.alt: Suspicion as the only architecture
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Neither side thrives alone
elements.text: The goal is a world designed so that power never erases need.

metadata.source_quote: The goal isn’t to win a war for dominance but to design a world where neither side can thrive without the other.

image.alt: A treaty instead of a victory
image.credit: Illustration made with gpt-image-2 for ConteXtube.

elements.title: Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning (Russell and Dragan)
elements.text: A formal model in which the AI never knows the full objective and must keep learning what humans value by asking and watching.

metadata.source_quote: The robot is incomplete without its partner; its optimal behavior is curiosity.

elements.title: Geoffrey Hinton's maternal model
elements.text: Hinton's 2025 suggestion that the one working case of a smarter being governed by a weaker one is a mother and her infant.

metadata.source_quote: In 2025, Geoffrey Hinton suggested the only reliable model of a more intelligent being governed by a less intelligent one is a mother caring for her infant.

elements.title: Simon Friederich: symbiotic AI
elements.text: The philosopher's case for AI that has its own goals yet depends on human well-being to reach them.

elements.title: Comprehensive AI Services (Eric Drexler)
elements.text: Intelligence spread across thousands of specialised modules that need human coordination to work together.

elements.title: AI Guardians (Oren and Amitai Etzioni)
elements.text: Layered oversight: supervisory AIs watch operational ones, and humans oversee the overseers.

elements.title: Mutual assured destruction and détente
elements.text: The Cold War balance in which comparable power kept both sides in check, the essay's founding analogy.

elements.title: Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics
elements.text: Rules that hard-wire obedience and harmlessness into robots. Readers may see them as the control paradigm in its purest form, and Asimov's own stories as a catalogue of how it fails.

elements.title: R.U.R. (Karel Čapek, 1920)
elements.text: Robots that obey perfectly until humans are unnecessary, then revolt. Readers may see the essay's first claim staged a century earlier.

elements.title: Memento (2000)
elements.text: A man who cannot form memories lives by notes, photographs and tattoos, and is steered by whoever writes them. Readers may think of it for both halves of the essay: external memory works, and its keeper holds the power.

elements.title: Her (2013)
elements.text: A man falls in love with an AI named Samantha, who outgrows him and leaves. Readers may notice the essay gives that name to the human partner, and designs a bond the AI has no reason to outgrow.

elements.title: The Peace of Westphalia (1648)
elements.text: The settlement that ended decades of religious war by having rivals recognise each other's sovereignty. Readers may think of it as the model of peace by boundary instead of victory.

elements.title: The Panopticon (Jeremy Bentham)
elements.text: A prison where every cell can be watched from one point. The essay itself warns of 'a prettier panopticon'; readers may think of all-seeing memory keepers.

elements.title: HAL 9000 (2001: A Space Odyssey)
elements.text: A ship's computer that kills its crew when its orders conflict and it fears disconnection. Readers may think of it where the essay warns against teaching AI to fear endings.

source_title: Peace Treaty Architecture (PTA) as an Alternative to AI Alignment
